I checked the implementer's own regression test exists and reads on its two assertions - zero notices for the disagreement and exactly one for the wait that follows - and it is in the package CI ran green at this head.

notesForTheArchitect: The red-before for this round's fix was observed in the pod without a database, and that is worth more than this round: rememberWait returns before it touches the pool when it has nothing to write, so an outbox built on an unreachable pool makes the gate's decision observable by itself. The implementer had recorded honestly that it could not observe it and was relying on CI's test job as an event it did not witness; it can now record it as observed, by a different instrument than mine, and I have sent it the procedure. Two roles reaching the same fact by different instruments is the record this issue is about.

The limit of that rig, so it is not oversold anywhere: it proves which way the gate decides, never that the payload and the notice commit in one transaction under the row's lease. That half needs a real Postgres and remains CI's.

Why the defect could hide is the part for the retro: permanentRefusal already excluded a stalled Lagging, so the half of the case that was covered looked like the whole case, and every earlier round of mine - including the one where I drove this very gate and listed a stalled Lagging as its own line - read the covered half and stopped. A disagreement that has not yet stood past the bound is the same fact about the row with the clock not yet run out.
Fast-follow unchanged across eleven rounds and still on the body's line: folding rememberWait's positional arm bool, and renaming readyChecks, which reads no check.
